Remark
[a minimiser is a reparametrised integral curve of $ abla r$]

Source: petersen:page-0195 ↗ rem:pet-ch5-distance-function-rigidity ↗ lem:pet-ch5-distance-function-segments

In the situation of section 3, put $L=L(c)|_a^b$ and $\varphi (s)=L(c)|_a^s=\int _a^s|\dot c|\, dt$, and suppose $\sigma :[0,L] o U$ is an integral curve of $ abla r$ with $\sigma (0)=c(a)$. Then $c=\sigma \circ \varphi $ on $[a,b]$: a curve realising the bound is a reparametrisation of an integral curve of $ abla r$.

Proof

↗ rem:pet-ch5-distance-function-rigidity \sketch By section 3, $\dot c=\varphi ' abla r$; also $\varphi (a)=0$ and $\varphi (b)=L$. The chain rule gives

\[ (\sigma \circ \varphi )'(s)=\varphi '(s)\, \dot\sigma (\varphi (s)) =\varphi '(s)\, abla r|_{\sigma (\varphi (s))}. \]

Thus $c$ and $\sigma \circ \varphi $ solve the same locally Lipschitz equation $y'=\varphi ' abla r(y)$ and agree at $a$; Grönwall uniqueness gives $c=\sigma \circ \varphi $. The map $\varphi $ is only nondecreasing, so rests of $c$ are allowed.

□
